canonical_statement: Baik--Deift--Johansson (1999), Theorem 1.1: if a permutation of N letters is uniformly distributed and L_N is the length of its longest strictly increasing subsequence, then for every real t, P((L_N - 2 sqrt(N))/N^(1/6) <= t) tends to F(t), where F is the Tracy--Widom distribution defined in source equations (1.4)--(1.6).

primary_source.authors: Jinho Baik, Percy Deift, Kurt Johansson
primary_source.title: On the distribution of the length of the longest increasing subsequence of random permutations

encoding_decisions.sample_space: Equiv.Perm (Fin N), with probability expressed as finite event cardinality divided by total cardinality
encoding_decisions.lis_statistic: supremum of cardinalities of Finset index sets on which the permutation is strictly increasing
encoding_decisions.normalization: ((lisLength sigma : Real) - 2 * Real.sqrt N) / (N : Real) ^ (1/6 : Real)
encoding_decisions.convergence: pointwise convergence of the cumulative probability for every real t
encoding_decisions.tracy_widom: existence of Airy Ai and the Hastings--McLeod Painleve II solution with the source asymptotics, followed by source formula (1.6)

mutation_tests: excluded the N = 0 indexing boundary by shifting N to N+1

computation_profile: noncomputable finite cardinalities, real improper integral, derivatives, and filter limits; no numerical computation or simulation receives proof credit
